subject: Clarify billing for mixed streaming + long-context usage
messages:

Cc: Anita Gomez <anita.gomez@novacorp.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Invoice spike — need clarity on minimums & rounding

Hi Stephanie,

We hope you’re well. We pulled our May invoice and saw a surprisingly large line-item labeled "context minimums" plus a rounding adjustment that looks like it increased billable units by ~12%. I attached the invoice (novacorp_invoice_202805.pdf) and our exported usage (usage_export_may.csv).

Two quick questions while we dig in:
- How are minimums applied when a single session mixes streaming calls (short requests) and one-off long-context embeddings (12k tokens)? Do those two use cases aggregate into the same "conversation window" or are they billed separately?
- The invoice shows a rounding "trigger" that bumped multiple small calls to a higher slab — is that floor applied per-request, per-minute, or after aggregation?

We’re trying to reconcile to our internal cost model and to scope any potential contract changes. If helpful, we can jump on a short call next week.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform — Novacorp
samir.patel@novacorp.com

Subject: Re: Invoice spike — need clarity on minimums & rounding

Hi Samir — thanks for the files. I took an initial pass and looped in Ben on pricing. Short answer: streaming short calls and long-context single-shot calls can be treated differently by our meter depending on how the calls are grouped and whether KV/prefix caching applies.

Preliminary notes:
- If requests share a conversation identifier and a client-side session persists KV cache, we try to aggregate tokens into the same conversation window (that can reduce billable units). If the long-context call is an independent request (no shared session ID), it will be billed as a separate session.
- Rounding: we apply a per-session rounding floor to the computed unit after aggregation; however there is also an account-level slabing step for invoices that can round up residuals when line items are below a threshold. That slabing is what likely created the ~12% uplift you saw.

I drafted some sample math and a breakdown in the attached workbook (math_workup.xlsx) and proposed a short call for Wednesday to walk through specifics. Ben — can you confirm the exact slab thresholds and whether Novacorp’s pilot contract qualifies for the pilot smoothing concession?

— Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

Attachments: math_workup.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Samir Patel <samir.patel@novacorp.com>

Subject: Re: Invoice spike — need clarity on minimums & rounding

Thanks for tagging me. I pulled account-level billing metadata for Novacorp. Key points and a worked example below.

Policy recap (concise):
- Aggregation boundary: tokens are first aggregated per conversation ID for the 24-hour rolling billing window. That gives per-session token totals.
- Per-session floor: after aggregation, we apply a per-session minimum (configurable by SKU). Default for your SKU is 100 units per session.
- Invoice-level smoothing: small residuals across sessions (<5% of monthly spend) can be bundled and rounded to simplify invoices; this is the slabing behavior Stephanie mentioned.

Worked example using your May export:
- You had 3,420 session IDs. Mean session tokens pre-aggregation: 78.
- After aggregation: 1,102 sessions remained under the 100-unit floor, which got each bumped to 100 units (that accounts for most of the uplift).
- Separately, a set of long-context one-offs (19 requests of ~12k tokens each) were billed as separate large sessions (no floor applied beyond the per-session calculation), so those are charged at actual units but still flowed into the monthly slabing step.

Suggestion: two mitigations we often use — 1) enable per-account prefix coalescing (collapses short bursts sharing the same prefix into a single session for billing purposes), and 2) increase the rolling-window to 72 hours for your integration to let sparse events aggregate more effectively. Both are non-invasive config flags and we can pilot them for June to see effect.

Concession ask: given this was the first invoice after a pilot change in ingestion, I recommend applying a one-time smoothing credit of up to 10% of the uplift while we run the pilot for June. If you’re okay with that, I’ll escalate to Marissa for approval.

— Ben
Ben Carter

ben_carter@redwood.com

- Activate prefix coalescing and 72-hour rolling window for Novacorp on a trial basis starting 2028-06-07.
- Share expected delta (estimate) vs May baseline by EOD Friday so Samir’s team can prep internal forecasts.

Samir — we’ll make the config change and monitor. If smoothing credit hits the cap we’ll follow the standard contract concession workflow.
